whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the Sharing and Visibility Architect exam?

personas.label: Admins focused on access control
personas.description: You configure profiles, roles, and sharing rules and want to design secure access for a larger org.

personas.label: Salesforce platform architects
personas.description: You are pursuing Application Architect, which includes the Sharing and Visibility Architect credential.

personas.label: Compliance specialists
personas.description: You need to explain which users can access records and why, including to auditors.

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the Sharing and Visibility Architect exam?
examDifficulty.summary: Questions ask you to diagnose why a person can or cannot access a record. You must identify the responsible layer, such as object permissions, org-wide defaults, the role hierarchy, sharing rules, teams, or Apex sharing.
bullets: 58% passing score, about 41 correct answers. Some options differ by one sharing setting.
External sharing matters. Review Experience Cloud sharing sets, external defaults, and guest-user rules.
Performance is tested. Learn how data skew, deep role hierarchies, and recalculations affect sharing.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Hands-on experience with sharing models helps. Before booking, aim for 75% on practice questions and be ready to trace why a user can access a record.

examFormat.heading: Sharing and Visibility Architect exam format
examFormat.intro: You may take the proctored exam online or at a test centre. Most questions describe a record-access scenario.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Scenarios ask which users need specific records and which records must remain hidden. Choose the simplest design that grants only the required access.
bestWayToPass: Start with private defaults: Set org-wide defaults to the narrowest access required, then grant access where needed.
Separate permission layers: Profiles and permission sets control objects and fields; sharing controls records.
Study external users separately: Customer Community, partner, and guest users have different sharing options.
Use Apex only for complex rules: Choose managed sharing when declarative options cannot express the requirement.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how you control access to Salesforce objects, fields, and records. Review org-wide defaults, roles, sharing rules, permission sets, external users, and performance. The exam is 60 scored questions in 120 minutes, with a 58% pass mark, weighted towards Access to Records (39%) and Permissions to Standard Objects, Custom Objects, and Fields (27%).

keyConcepts.h2: Sharing and Visibility Architect: concepts to review

blocks.heading: Org-wide defaults set the baseline
blocks.body: Org-wide defaults (OWD) set the starting record access for an object: Private, Public Read Only, or Public Read/Write. Sharing mechanisms can grant more access but cannot remove access already granted by OWD. Start with the most restrictive level users need, then open access for other groups. Detail records in a master-detail relationship inherit access from the parent. Internal and external defaults may differ, but external access cannot be broader than internal access.

blocks.heading: Sharing through roles, rules, and teams
blocks.body: The role hierarchy can grant managers access to records owned below them. For custom objects, Grant Access Using Hierarchies may be turned off. Owner-based rules share by record owner; criteria-based rules share based on a field value. Account, Opportunity, and Case teams grant access to named people on a record. Manual shares are removed when ownership changes. Apex managed sharing handles more complex requirements and can persist after ownership changes when configured with a custom sharing reason.

blocks.heading: External user access
blocks.body: Experience Cloud users follow separate sharing options. Customer Community users do not have roles; sharing sets can grant access to records related to their Account or Contact. Share groups can extend access to internal users connected to those records. Partner and Customer Community Plus users have roles and can be included in sharing rules. Guest users are unauthenticated and have Private defaults; use guest user sharing rules to give them access. Check that internal sharing does not expose records externally.

blocks.heading: Object, field, and record permissions
blocks.body: Record sharing determines which rows a user may access. Object and field permissions control access to objects and columns. Every user has one profile; keep it minimal and add access with permission sets and permission set groups. A muting permission set can remove permissions granted through a group. Field-level security applies to pages, reports, list views, and APIs. Restriction rules can narrow visible records even when sharing would allow more.

blocks.heading: Performance and audit
blocks.body: Sharing recalculation can slow when one user owns many records or a parent has many child records. Ownership and account data skew can also cause locks. Distribute ownership where possible, place integration users outside the role hierarchy when appropriate, and defer sharing calculations during large changes. A record’s Sharing view explains access. Setup Audit Trail tracks configuration changes; Field History Tracking and Shield Field Audit Trail track data changes.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Sharing and Visibility Architect exam
scenarioTips.intro: Identify who needs access, which records they need, and whether the users are internal or external. Then choose the narrowest setting that meets the requirement.

blocks.heading: Trace the access layers
blocks.body: Check object permissions first, then the record baseline and applicable sharing. Sharing cannot grant access to an object the user cannot read.

blocks.heading: Choose sharing rules by their basis
blocks.body: Use criteria-based rules when access depends on a field value and owner-based rules when it depends on record ownership. Formula fields are not supported in criteria-based rules.

blocks.heading: Separate external user types
blocks.body: Customer Community users use sharing sets and share groups. Partner and Customer Community Plus users can use roles and sharing rules. Guest users need guest user sharing rules.

blocks.heading: Recognize data skew
blocks.body: One owner with many records or one Account with many child records can slow sharing calculations. Consider ownership distribution and deferred recalculation.

blocks.heading: Use Apex for complex sharing
blocks.body: Use Apex managed sharing when configuration cannot express the rule, such as access based on a related record. A custom sharing reason can preserve shares after owner changes.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Architect Certifications
nextCertsAfter.intro: Build on your security architecture knowledge with these related Salesforce credentials:

sampleQuestions.question: Sales reps should see only their Opportunities, while managers can see their teams’ records. What is a suitable starting setup?
options: Private OWD with manual sharing set up by hand for each record
Public Read Only OWD and a manager sharing rule
Private OWD with manager access through the role hierarchy
Public Read/Write OWD with field-level security
sampleQuestions.explanation: Private OWD limits peer visibility, while the role hierarchy can grant managers access to records owned by their teams.
whyWrong: Manual shares are hard to maintain and can be removed when ownership changes.
Public Read Only exposes other reps’ records.
Field security hides fields, not records.

sampleQuestions.question: A user sees an Account in a list but cannot open a related custom object record. What should the architect check first?
options: The Account sharing rules for the user's role
The user’s role
The org login IP ranges
Read permission on the custom object
sampleQuestions.explanation: Object permission is required before record sharing can grant access.
whyWrong: The user can already view the Account, so its access is working.
A role affects record access but does not grant object permission.
An IP range would affect login, not just a single object.

sampleQuestions.question: Cases with Region = EMEA must be shared with the EMEA Support group regardless of owner. Which feature fits?
options: Public Read Only Case OWD
A Case team on every record
A criteria-based Case sharing rule
An owner-based Case sharing rule for EMEA
sampleQuestions.explanation: The criteria is a field value rather than the record owner, so use criteria-based sharing.
whyWrong: Public Read Only would expose all Cases.
Adding teams to every Case is difficult to maintain.
Owner-based rules depend on who owns each record.

sampleQuestions.question: Customer Community users should view Cases related to their Account, but they do not have roles. What should be configured?
options: A sharing set that matches the user’s Account to the Case
A permission set with View All on Case
A criteria-based sharing rule covering all community users
The role hierarchy
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sharing sets grant Customer Community users access to records related to their Account or Contact.
whyWrong: View All would expose Cases across the org.
These users lack roles and cannot use most role-based sharing rules.
The role hierarchy does not apply to role-less community users.

sampleQuestions.question: An integration user owns two million Accounts, and role updates now take hours. What is the likely cause?
options: Too many profiles
Ownership data skew on that user
Too many permission set groups in use
Field security on Account
sampleQuestions.explanation: When one user owns many records, role changes can trigger large sharing recalculations.
whyWrong: Profile count does not cause record sharing recalculation.
Permission set groups control object and field access.
Field security does not calculate record sharing.

sampleQuestions.question: Project access must be granted to users listed in a related Project Member object, and the list changes often. What should the architect use?
options: An owner-based sharing rule
Public Read/Write Project OWD
Apex managed sharing with a custom sharing reason
Manual sharing by the project owner each time the list changes
sampleQuestions.explanation: The access depends on records in another object, which declarative sharing cannot express. Apex managed sharing can implement it and preserve shares after ownership changes.
whyWrong: Owner-based rules cannot read the related member list.
Public sharing grants access to everyone.
Manual shares require ongoing effort and are removed when ownership changes.

sampleQuestions.question: Managers should not inherit automatic access to records for a custom object. Which setting should change?
options: Remove Read permission from their profile
Remove their role from the hierarchy and assign access with a profile
Add a restriction rule
Turn off Grant Access Using Hierarchies for the object
sampleQuestions.explanation: This custom-object setting prevents automatic access through the role hierarchy.
whyWrong: This removes all object access, including access the manager may need.
Removing the role affects access across many objects.
The hierarchy setting directly addresses the stated need.

sampleQuestions.question: Which statement about internal and external org-wide defaults is true?
options: Sharing rules can reduce access below OWD
External OWD can be more open than internal OWD
Permission sets grant access to individual records
External OWD cannot be more open than internal OWD
sampleQuestions.explanation: External defaults must be the same as or more restrictive than internal defaults.
whyWrong: Sharing rules grant access and do not take it away.
External defaults cannot be broader.
Permission sets grant object and field permissions, not individual record access.

sampleQuestions.question: Partner users should see Opportunities owned by users at their own partner company, but not other companies. What should be configured?
options: Public Read Only Opportunity OWD
A sharing rule using partner-account roles
A sharing set for the partner users’ profile
View All on Opportunities
sampleQuestions.explanation: Partner users have roles under their partner account, which can be used in a sharing rule for that company.
whyWrong: Public access would expose records to all partner companies.
Sharing sets are intended for Customer Community users.
View All exposes all Opportunities.

sampleQuestions.question: Reps can currently see every Invoice because of a broad sharing rule. They should see only invoices for their country without redesigning the model. Which feature can narrow visibility?
options: A muting permission set
A restriction rule
A criteria-based sharing rule
Field-level security
sampleQuestions.explanation: Restriction rules filter which records users can see even if sharing grants broader access.
whyWrong: Muting permissions change object or field permissions, not record visibility.
Sharing rules add access rather than remove it.
Field security hides fields, not records.

sampleQuestions.question: Anonymous visitors should read selected records on a public Experience Cloud site. How should access be granted?
options: A guest user sharing rule
A role-hierarchy assignment
Public Read Only external OWD
A regular public group
sampleQuestions.explanation: Guest users have private defaults; grant record access through guest user sharing rules.
whyWrong: Guest users do not have roles.
Guest defaults cannot be opened this way.
Guest users cannot be placed in regular public groups for record sharing.

sampleQuestions.question: A manual share gives a colleague access to an Opportunity. The record later changes owners. What happens to the share?
options: It transfers to the new owner
It stays only if the users share a role
It turns into a sharing rule
It is removed
sampleQuestions.explanation: Manual shares are removed when record ownership changes. Apex managed sharing with a custom reason can preserve a programmed share.
whyWrong: Manual shares do not transfer automatically.
The colleague’s role does not preserve the manual share.
A manual share does not become a sharing rule.

sampleQuestions.question: The org will load five million records and change sharing rules. How can the team avoid repeated recalculations during the work?
options: Turn off hierarchy access globally
Make OWD Public Read/Write
Defer Sharing Calculations, then recalculate after the load
Delete and recreate all sharing rules after each batch of records loads
sampleQuestions.explanation: Deferring calculations lets the large data and configuration changes complete before recalculation.
whyWrong: This is not a global option for all standard objects and could change access.
Opening access can expose data.
Deleting and recreating rules may cause multiple expensive recalculations.

sampleQuestions.question: An agent can edit Case Status but must not see a Contact’s Social Security number. Which setting controls that field?
options: Field-level security
Org-wide defaults
A record sharing rule
Role hierarchy
sampleQuestions.explanation: Field-level security controls visibility and edit access for a field, including in reports and APIs.
whyWrong: OWD controls record access rather than field visibility.
Sharing rules grant record access, not field access.
The role hierarchy grants record access, not field access.

sampleQuestions.question: An auditor asks why a user can open one Account. Where should the admin check first?
options: The Sharing details on that Account
A report showing the user’s profile
Every sharing rule exported for the org
The user’s login history
sampleQuestions.explanation: The record’s Sharing view shows who has access and the reason, such as a rule, team, or ownership.
whyWrong: A profile report shows object permissions, not why this record is visible.
Reading every rule is slow and may miss teams and manual shares.
Login history does not explain record access.
